Class StackListIteratorTest

java.lang.Object
myTest.StackListIteratorTest
public class StackListIteratorTest extends Object
Summary: This Test Suite verifies the behavior of the bidirectional HListIterator implementation within the StackAdapter. The suite is divided into sections using comments to group tests by the method being tested. The tests check how to go backwards, track the index, and change items in the list, maintaining compatibility with the J2SE 1.4.2 collections framework.
  • Test Case Design: The tests have been developed following the Test Driven Development methodology, meaning they were implemented before their respective methods. The goal is to validate the cursor position during multiple forward/backward movements, and to ensure that insertions and removals correctly update the underlying stack while respecting the limits of J2SE 1.4.2.

Conventions used in the documentation of the tests:

  • Every test starts from the same state: setUp() creates a new, empty StackAdapter (stackTest) before each test, so the Pre-Condition of every test is an empty stack and all the elements used are inserted by the test itself (as described in its Test Description).
  • The content of a stack is written from the bottom (index 0) to the top, e.g. [A, B] means that "A" was pushed first and "B" is on top. The iterators traverse the stack in the same order.

    • testHasPreviousOnEmptyStack

      public void testHasPreviousOnEmptyStack()
      Summary: Verifies that hasPrevious() returns false on an HListIterator obtained from an empty stack.
      • Test Case Design: Empty collection.
      • Test Description: Calls listIterator() on the empty stack and then calls hasPrevious().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is still empty; the cursor is at index 0.
      • Expected Results: hasPrevious() returns false.

    • testHasPreviousRegularBehavior

      public void testHasPreviousRegularBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that hasPrevious() returns true after the cursor has moved forward.
      • Test Case Design: Standard case: cursor between the first and the second element.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B", creates an HListIterator with listIterator(), calls next() (returns "A") and then calls hasPrevious().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged ([A, B]); the cursor is at index 1, between "A" and "B".
      • Expected Results: hasPrevious() returns true.

    • testHasPreviousAtStartReturnsFalse

      public void testHasPreviousAtStartReturnsFalse()
      Summary: Verifies that hasPrevious() returns false when the cursor is at the beginning of a non-empty stack.
      • Test Case Design: Boundary case: cursor at index 0 with elements available only in the forward direction.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B", creates an HListIterator with listIterator() and calls hasPrevious() without moving the cursor.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged ([A, B]); the cursor is at index 0.
      • Expected Results: hasPrevious() returns false.

    • testHasPreviousAfterNextAndPrevious

      public void testHasPreviousAfterNextAndPrevious()
      Summary: Verifies that hasPrevious() follows the cursor when it moves forward and then back.
      • Test Case Design: Cursor state tracking during a forward step followed by a backward step.
      • Test Description: Pushes the String "A", creates an HListIterator, calls next() and asserts that hasPrevious() is true; then calls previous() (returns "A") and asserts that hasPrevious() is false.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged ([A]); the cursor is back at index 0.
      • Expected Results: hasPrevious() returns true after next() and false after previous().

    • testHasPreviousContinuousCheck

      public void testHasPreviousContinuousCheck()
      Summary: Verifies that consecutive calls to hasPrevious() do not move the cursor.
      • Test Case Design: Checks that hasPrevious() is a pure query with no side effects.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B", creates an HListIterator with listIterator(2) (cursor at the end) and calls hasPrevious() three times in a row.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged ([A, B]); the cursor is still at index 2.
      • Expected Results: All three calls return true.

    • testPreviousStandardBehavior

      public void testPreviousStandardBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that previous() called right after next() returns the same element.
      • Test Case Design: Standard return value of previous(): alternating next() and previous() returns the same element.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B", creates an HListIterator, stores the result of next() ("A") and the result of the following previous(), then compares the two values.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged ([A, B]); the cursor is back at index 0.
      • Expected Results: Both calls return "A", so the two stored values are equal.

    • testPreviousOnMultipleCallsReturnBackwardOrder

      public void testPreviousOnMultipleCallsReturnBackwardOrder()
      Summary: Verifies that repeated calls to previous() return the elements in reverse order.
      • Test Case Design: Complete backward traversal starting from the end of the list.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B" and "C", creates an HListIterator with listIterator(3) (cursor after the last element) and calls previous() three times.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged ([A, B, C]); the cursor is at index 0.
      • Expected Results: previous() returns "C", "B" and "A" in this order.

    • testListIteratorRemoveWithoutNextOrPreviousThrowsIllegalStateException

      public void testListIteratorRemoveWithoutNextOrPreviousThrowsIllegalStateException()
      Summary: Verifies that remove() on an HListIterator throws IllegalStateException if neither next() nor previous() has been called.
      • Test Case Design: Exception handling: an HListIterator created in the middle of a list has no last returned element.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B", creates an HListIterator with listIterator(1) and immediately calls remove().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged: [A, B].
      • Expected Results: A myAdapter.IllegalStateException is thrown.

    • testRemoveAfterPreviousRemovesTopElement

      public void testRemoveAfterPreviousRemovesTopElement()
      Summary: Verifies that remove() after previous() deletes the element returned by previous(), here the top of the stack.
      • Test Case Design: Backward removal at the end of the list.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B" and "C", creates an HListIterator with listIterator(3), calls previous() (checking it returns "C") and remove(). Then checks size() and peek() on the stack, and hasNext() and nextIndex() on the HListIterator.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains two elements: [A, B]; the cursor is at index 2 (end of the list).
      • Expected Results: size() returns 2, peek() returns "B", hasNext() returns false and nextIndex() returns 2.

    • testRemoveAfterPreviousInTheMiddle

      public void testRemoveAfterPreviousInTheMiddle()
      Summary: Verifies that remove() after previous() deletes an element in the middle and leaves the cursor in the right position.
      • Test Case Design: Backward removal in the middle of the list and cursor consistency afterwards.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B" and "C", creates an HListIterator with listIterator(3), calls previous() twice (returns "C", then "B") and remove() (removes "B"). Then checks size(), get(0) and get(1) on the stack, and nextIndex() and next() on the HListIterator.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains two elements: [A, C]; after the final next() the cursor is at index 2.
      • Expected Results: size() returns 2, get(0) returns "A", get(1) returns "C", nextIndex() returns 1 and next() returns "C".

    • testRemoveAfterPreviousAtFirstElement

      public void testRemoveAfterPreviousAtFirstElement()
      Summary: Verifies that remove() after previous() deletes the first element (bottom of the stack).
      • Test Case Design: Backward removal at index 0.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B" and "C", creates an HListIterator with listIterator(1), calls previous() (checking it returns "A") and remove(). Then checks size() and get(0) on the stack, and hasPrevious(), nextIndex() and next() on the HListIterator.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains two elements: [B, C]; after the final next() the cursor is at index 1.
      • Expected Results: size() returns 2, get(0) returns "B", hasPrevious() returns false, nextIndex() returns 0 and next() returns "B".

    • testRemoveAllElementsBackward

      public void testRemoveAllElementsBackward()
      Summary: Verifies that calling previous() and remove() on every element, starting from the end, empties the stack.
      • Test Case Design: Multiple consecutive removals during a complete backward scan.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Integers 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, creates an HListIterator with listIterator(stackTest.size()) and, while hasPrevious() is true, calls previous() and remove(), counting the removals. Then checks the counter and isEmpty().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is empty.
      • Expected Results: Exactly 5 removals are performed and isEmpty() returns true.

    • testRemoveTwiceAfterPreviousThrowsIllegalStateException

      public void testRemoveTwiceAfterPreviousThrowsIllegalStateException()
      Summary: Verifies that two remove() calls after a single previous() throw IllegalStateException.
      • Test Case Design: Exception handling in the backward direction: each previous() allows at most one remove().
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B", creates an HListIterator with listIterator(2), calls previous() (returns "B"), remove() (removes "B") and then remove() again.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: Only the first remove() has taken effect: the stack contains only "A".
      • Expected Results: The first remove() succeeds; the second throws a myAdapter.IllegalStateException.

    • testRemoveMixedDirections

      public void testRemoveMixedDirections()
      Summary: Verifies remove() when forward and backward movements are mixed.
      • Test Case Design: Removal after next() followed by removal after previous(), in two different positions of the same list.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B", "C" and "D" and creates an HListIterator. Calls next() twice (returns "A" and "B") and remove() (removes "B"); then calls previous() (checking it returns "A") and remove() (removes "A"). Finally checks next(), size(), get(0) and get(1).
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains two elements: [C, D]; after the final next() the cursor is at index 1.
      • Expected Results: previous() returns "A", the final next() returns "C", size() returns 2, get(0) returns "C" and get(1) returns "D".

      • Test Description: Pushes the String "A", creates an HListIterator, calls next() (returns "A"), calls add("B") and then calls set("C").
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.

      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B", creates an HListIterator, calls next() (returns "A") and then set("C"); finally calls contains("A"), contains("C") and size() on the stack.

      public void testSetReplaceElementAfterPrevious()
      Summary: Verifies that set(Object) replaces the element returned by previous().
      • Test Case Design: Standard replacement after a backward step.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B", creates an HListIterator with listIterator(2), calls previous() (returns "B") and then set("C"); finally calls peek() and size() on the stack.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains two elements: [A, C].
      • Expected Results: peek() returns "C" and size() returns 2.

    • testRemoveAfterAddThrowsIllegalStateException

      public void testRemoveAfterAddThrowsIllegalStateException()
      Summary: Verifies that remove() throws IllegalStateException if called right after add(Object), also when the cursor was moved with previous().
      • Test Case Design: Exception handling: add() invalidates the last returned element for remove() too (testSetAfterAddThrowsIllegalStateException covers set()), reached through a backward movement instead of a forward one.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B", creates an HListIterator with listIterator(2), calls previous() (returns "B"), then add("C") (inserted at index 1, before "B") and finally remove().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains three elements: [A, C, B] (add() succeeded, remove() had no effect).
      • Expected Results: A myAdapter.IllegalStateException is thrown by remove().

    • testAddOnEmptyStack

      public void testAddOnEmptyStack()
      Summary: Verifies that add(Object) on an HListIterator of an empty stack inserts the element.
      • Test Case Design: Insertion into an empty collection.
      • Test Description: Calls listIterator() on the empty stack, calls add("A"), then calls size() and contains("A") on the stack.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains one element: [A]; the cursor is at index 1.
      • Expected Results: size() returns 1 and contains("A") returns true.

    • testAddRegularBehavior

      public void testAddRegularBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that add(Object) inserts the element immediately before the cursor and moves the cursor after it.
      • Test Case Design: Positional accuracy of the insertion in the middle of the list.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B", creates an HListIterator with listIterator(1) (cursor between "A" and "B") and calls add("C"). Then calls previous() and checks it returns "C"; calls next() (returns "C" again, value not checked) and then next() and checks it returns "B"; finally calls size() on the stack.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains three elements: [A, C, B]; the cursor is at index 3 (end of the list).
      • Expected Results: previous() returns "C", the last next() returns "B" and size() returns 3.

    • testAddNullElement

      public void testAddNullElement()
      Summary: Verifies that add(Object) accepts a null element.

      • Post-Condition: The stack contains one element: [null].

    • testAddDifferentTypes

      public void testAddDifferentTypes()
      Summary: Verifies that consecutive add(Object) calls insert elements of different types in order.
      • Test Case Design: Heterogeneous elements; each insertion is placed after the previous one because the cursor moves forward.
      • Test Description: Calls listIterator() on the empty stack and then add(1), add("Hi") and add('A'); finally calls size(), peek(), contains(1) and contains("Hi") on the stack.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains three elements: [1, "Hi", 'A'].
      • Expected Results: size() returns 3, peek() returns 'A', contains(1) and contains("Hi") return true.
